clue.text: Purcell has composed, despite being gloomy

indicators.note: composed means put together or arranged, so the letters of the composer's name and the next word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Henry Purcell wrote his music in spite of a melancholy disposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has composed' looks like it describes Purcell's work, but 'composed' is the signal to rearrange PURCELL plus HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sepulchral suggests a tomb, so it is dismal and funereal in mood.

clue.text: Not all convicts in gaol turn informer

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not every prisoner in jail will grass on fellow inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: To sing is slang for confessing or giving evidence against accomplices to the police.

clue.text: Bet you'll find one on the cam!

definitions.meaning: a ... is a wager, especially a small speculative one
a flat-bottomed boat poled along the River Cam in Cambridge

explanation.surface: A cheery tip that a wager can be found on a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The lower-case 'cam' hides the River Cam, which flows through Cambridge, where students pole flat boats along the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a gamble placed with a bookmaker, and a long shallow boat propelled with a pole.

clue.text: Refuse to take a chair

definitions.meaning: refuse as a noun means rubbish scattered about
a curtained chair or couch carried on poles

explanation.surface: Declining to sit down when offered a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb (decline) but is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is strewn rubbish, and also a historical carried seat like a sedan.

clue.text: Brief tyranny admitting no deviation

parts.note: a regulation that is harsh and quick, a severe short reign, yet in normal speech a strict principle with no exceptions

explanation.surface: A short, harsh dictatorship that tolerates no dissent.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, a 'brief tyranny' is a rule that is both hard (harsh) and fast (quick); the plain meaning is a fixed principle allowing no exceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a fixed regulation that must be followed exactly, with no exceptions allowed.

clue.text: Get justice for archdeacon in time

indicators.note: in places the churchman's title inside the word for an era

parts.note: an age is a period of time
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon in the Church of England

explanation.surface: An archdeacon finally obtains redress in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is addressed as 'the Venerable', abbreviated VEN; it goes inside AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to exact retribution or satisfaction on behalf of the victim.

clue.text: Hard worker, but utterly sullen

indicators.note: utterly is read as 'when uttered', so the word for sullen is spoken out loud

parts.note: dour means stern and sullen

explanation.surface: A diligent employee who is nevertheless thoroughly grumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utterly' looks like an intensifier ('completely sullen') but means 'when spoken': DOUR pronounced 'doo-er' sounds like DOER.
explanation.definitionFit: A doer is an active, practical person who gets things done rather than just talking.

clue.text: It's anything but rare

parts.note: rare suggests uncommon, but here it means lightly cooked meat, and the opposite is meat left on the heat far too long

explanation.surface: Something that is extremely common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rare' seems to mean scarce; it is the steak sense, underdone.
explanation.definitionFit: Food cooked far past done is the extreme opposite of a bloody, underdone steak.

clue.text: Failing parishes do need to show enthusiasm

indicators.note: failing parishes are in disarray, so the letters of parishes and do are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Struggling church districts really must display some zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like an emphatic auxiliary ('do need') but is part of the letters rearranged with PARISHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhapsodise is to speak or write with great excitement and effusive praise.

clue.text: No French hors d'oeuvre for total loser

parts.note: non is the French word for no
a starter is the first course of a meal, an appetiser

explanation.surface: Declining the appetiser, perhaps at a French restaurant, marks one as a failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-hoper with no chance of success is described idiomatically as a nonstarter.

clue.text: Handsome Parisian meets a Hungarian

parts.note: bel is a French form of beautiful or handsome, as in bel homme

explanation.surface: A good-looking Frenchman is introduced to a man from Budapest.
explanation.walkthrough: BELA is a common Hungarian male name, as with the composer Béla Bartók.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla is a typical Magyar first name, so it stands for a person from Hungary.

clue.text: What Marx wrote about the money invested in Germany

definitions.meaning: Karl Marx's economic treatise criticising capitalism
in German the phrase literally means 'the capital', capital being money invested

explanation.surface: Marx's book was concerned with funds put into German industry.
explanation.walkthrough: The German title translates as 'Capital', which is also money used for investment.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx's famous economic work bears this German title, meaning 'capital' as in invested wealth.

clue.text: Memorable mention about a prince introducing poll-tax

indicators.note: about means the commendation goes around the short article and the royal abbreviation

parts.note: a citation is an honourable mention, as in a military commendation

explanation.surface: A notable reference to royalty introduces a much-hated tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tells us CITATION wraps round A + P, splitting after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitation is a levy of a fixed sum per head of population, which is what a poll tax charges.

clue.text: Madden the German with unending rage

parts.note: der is a German word for the

indicators.note: unending says the synonym for fury loses its final letter

parts.note: anger is another word for rage

explanation.surface: Infuriate the German by showing him endless fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rage' is not cut itself: its synonym ANGER loses its last letter, giving ANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange someone is to drive them mad, which is one sense of madden.

clue.text: Expert fish worker

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
a hand is a manual labourer, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A skilled fisherman or fishmonger at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab hand is British slang for someone highly skilled at something.

clue.text: Emerge slowly to remove opponents

definitions.meaning: to come out by inching forward gradually
to beat rivals narrowly and force them out of contention

explanation.surface: Cautiously coming out from cover in order to oust rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both creeping out gradually and narrowly displacing a competitor.

clue.text: A vice-admiral and rating of divine appearance

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for vice-admiral
a rating is an ordinary sailor, and a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: A senior naval officer and an ordinary seaman look godlike.
explanation.walkthrough: In naval terms a 'rating' is a sailor who is not an officer; TAR is an old word for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief an avatar is the incarnation of a deity in bodily form on earth.

clue.text: Reasons why Italian leader is welcomed by English head of state

indicators.note: being welcomed by is being taken in, so the dictator's title goes between the other letters
head of means the first letter of the word state

parts.note: Il Duce, meaning the leader, was Mussolini's title

explanation.surface: Explaining why an Italian prime minister was received by the British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of state' looks like a monarch or president, but here it just gives the S from 'state'.
explanation.definitionFit: To educe is to deduce or infer, drawing a conclusion out by reasoning.

clue.text: Think of goatherd made vagrant

indicators.note: made means formed into something new, so the letters are rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Imagine a goat-keeper reduced to a life of wandering.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight of the road is a jocular term for a tramp or wandering homeless person.

clue.text: Intends taking one in the lowlands

indicators.note: taking means the word for intends takes in another letter

parts.note: plans means intends
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone means to bring a person into the low country.
explanation.definitionFit: Plains are broad flat areas of low-lying land.

clue.text: A shade insane, sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who is a bit mad, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A shade insane' reads as 'slightly mad', but 'A shade' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earthy brownish-orange pigment and colour.

clue.text: Force top unionist to appear fully clothed!

indicators.note: to appear in, so the leading letter is placed inside the word for clothing

parts.note: dress means clothing, as in full dress

indicators.note: top means the first letter of unionist

explanation.surface: A leading trade unionist is compelled to turn up in proper attire.
explanation.walkthrough: The U from 'top unionist' appears inside DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion by threats or violence.

clue.text: He's wearing women's clothes, the monster!

parts.note: drag is women's clothing worn by a man
having something on means wearing it

explanation.surface: Exclaiming at a man dressed as a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: With DRAG ON, he 'has drag on', so the man is wearing women's clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a mythical fire-breathing beast.

clue.text: To misrepresent daughter is wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: It is wrong to give a false picture of one's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: TORT is a legal term for a civil wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort facts is to twist them into a false account.

clue.text: Stylish haircut

definitions.meaning: a light cut to tidy the hair

explanation.surface: A fashionable hairdo.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim means smart and tidy, and also a brief cut at the barber's.

clue.text: In oran illustrious people wear blue

indicators.note: In means the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Distinguished folk in Oran dress in blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Oran is a port city in Algeria.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the blue dye made from it.

clue.text: Conscription is a duty

definitions.meaning: a body of troops called up, or raising them
a tax or charge imposed by authority

explanation.surface: Military call-up is an obligation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duty' reads as an obligation but means a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Levy means both enlisting troops and an imposed tax.

clue.text: Self-gratification requires forgiveness

definitions.meaning: in the medieval church, a remission of punishment for sins

explanation.surface: Treating oneself requires being pardoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence means pampering oneself, and also a church pardon remitting the penalty for sin.

clue.text: Work for the railway

definitions.meaning: a ... of work is an occupation

explanation.surface: Being employed by a train company.
explanation.definitionFit: Line means a trade or occupation, and a stretch of rail track.

clue.text: Early plant produced with fatherly care

indicators.note: produced means made out of raw material, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gardener nurses a young seedling like a father.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting paternally means behaving as a protective father would.
